questions.q: In the ninety-day plan, why does the Windows work start with an AD and permissions inventory before any GPO baseline is applied?
options: You need to know what's actually drifted — domain structure, group membership, NTFS/share permissions — before you can fix it with a baseline
GPOs can only be applied after all servers are patched
Active Directory inventories are unrelated to GPO baselines
Inventory is a Linux-only concept covered in Chapter 4
questions.explain: You can't correctly scope a hardening baseline without first knowing what the current, drifted state of AD and permissions actually is.

questions.q: Which chapters cover the Linux hardening work described in weeks three and four of the plan?
options: Chapters 4 and 5 — Linux administration deep dive, and Linux hardening & security tools
Chapters 1 and 2 — Windows Server/AD fundamentals and Group Policy
Chapter 8 only — the capstone chapter introduces all Linux concepts for the first time
Chapter 6 — Patch management covers all Linux hardening
questions.explain: Sudoers, PAM, file permissions, and cron/timer security are Chapter 4; SELinux/AppArmor, auditd, SSH, and fail2ban are Chapter 5.

questions.q: Why does the plan treat an asset inventory as part of the ongoing endpoint-protection work, rather than a one-time setup task?
options: Because none of the hardening or patching work protects a server that isn't known to exist in the first place
Because asset inventories replace the need for patch management
Because asset inventory is only relevant to Windows, not Linux
Because EDR tools automatically discover and inventory assets with no ongoing effort
questions.explain: An accurate, maintained asset inventory is what makes sure every server is actually covered by patching, hardening, and endpoint protection.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes the environment ready for the next external review by day ninety?
options: It's documented and auditable, not just patched — every fix is verifiable, which is what Lesson 31's case study showed was missing
Every server has been completely reinstalled from scratch
All Linux servers have been migrated to Windows for consistency
The company skips the next audit entirely
questions.explain: Documentation and auditability, not just the underlying fixes, are what prevent a repeat of the kind of findings Lesson 31 walked through.

questions.q: What course comes next in this career path after Windows, Linux & Security Administration is complete?
options: Network Security, Endpoint Protection & Threat Detection
IT, Networking & Cybersecurity Fundamentals
There is no further course in this path
Advanced Databricks & Delta Lake
questions.explain: This lesson's outro names Network Security, Endpoint Protection & Threat Detection as the next course in the Cybersecurity Analyst to Security Engineer path.
